answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a atlas as the anchor of the cost.
